title: Check your understanding: Git's Content-Addressable Storage

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of git's content-addressable storage?
options: Git object IDs are derived from object content and type, which lets Git identify and verify stored objects. A hash is not a file path, author name or a cryptographic guarantee that every external workflow is trustworthy.
Git automatically backs up every file, including ignored and untracked files, to a remote.
The operation grants every contributor write access to the hosted repository.
questions.answer_key: Git object IDs are derived from object content and type, which lets Git identify and verify stored objects. A hash is not a file path, author name or a cryptographic guarantee that every external workflow is trustworthy.
questions.explanation: Git object IDs are derived from object content and type, which lets Git identify and verify stored objects. A hash is not a file path, author name or a cryptographic guarantee that every external workflow is trustworthy.

questions.prompt: Which command is the most direct starting point for this lesson’s example?
questions.explanation: Use `git hash-object README.md` as the first inspection/action in the example, and then verify the result with the companion checks in the lesson.

questions.prompt: Which is the safest general practice when working with git's content-addressable storage?
options: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
Run the most destructive option first; the reflog guarantees every file can always be recovered.
Assume the local command also changed the remote and satisfied all hosting-platform policies.
questions.answer_key: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
questions.explanation: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
